panels.rationale: Single-panel clinical photograph of a real patient's left foot/ankle showing erythematous, scaly eczematous lesions (arrows). The caption and article title explicitly attribute the eczema to Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome cutaneous manifestations, and the in-text describes diffuse eczema in this WAS case report. Eczematous dermatitis is a classic WAS manifestation; the image clearly shows skin of a light-skinned child patient. Prior caption triage also flagged this as a clear disease manifestation with no third-party concern.

in_text_mentions: Physical examination revealed severe failure to thrive, marked mucocutaneous pallor, and hepatosplenomegaly extending approximately 2 cm below the costal margin. Diffuse eczema consisting of widespread pruritic erythematous and scaly lesions was observed (Figure 1), together with cutaneous hemorrhagic manifestations in the form of petechiae (Figure 2).

panels.rationale: Clinical photograph showing healed hypo- and hyperpigmented scaly lesions on the trunk and extremities of a pediatric patient diagnosed with Wiskott-Aldrich Syndrome. The eczematous dermatitis of WAS is a classic manifestation, and the healed pigmentary changes with scaling are consistent with resolved WAS-related eczematous dermatitis. The skin tone visible in the image is dark (Fitzpatrick V-VI), consistent with the patient's Ethiopian background. The image clearly shows a real human patient with a specific clinical manifestation of the target disease.
panels.attribution_text: Deribssa and Alemayehu. A Clinical Diagnosis of Wiskott Aldrich Syndrome in an Ethiopian Boy with Recurrent Sinopulmonary Infections: A Case Report.. Ethiopian journal of health sciences 2020. doi:10.4314/ejhs.v30i6.26. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: Healed hypo-and hyperpigmented, scaly lesions on the trunk and extremities)
in_text_mentions: appeared chronically sick with extensive skin lesions but no dysmorphia. His pulse rate was 108/minute, respiratory rate 52/minute, temperature 36.4oC and saturation of oxygen in room air of 82%. He was underweight (weight = 12 kg). He had profuse purulent discharge from his right ear with an excoriated right pinna. He had no oral thrush. He had submandibular lymphadenopathy and hepatomegaly of 12 cm. He had crusted lesions on the scalp and face (Figure 1) and hypopigmented lesions on trunk and extremities (Figure 2). He also hadumblicated small nodules over face and extremities and clubbing.

panels.rationale: Real clinical photograph of a human patient's bilateral feet showing chronic eczematous lesions with excoriation, crusting and hyperpigmentation. Eczematous dermatitis is a hallmark manifestation of Wiskott-Aldrich Syndrome, and the article title confirms WAS unmasked in adulthood. The image is clear, adequately lit, free of annotations or third-party markings; disease attribution and finding are well supported.

On physical examination, diffuse eczema was observed (Figure 1), along with widespread petechiae and pulmonary crepitant rales and rhonchi. His family history was unremarkable. Laboratory analysis revealed anemia (hemoglobin of 8.9 g/dL), leukocytosis (white blood count of 13,330/mm3), andthrombocytopenia (platelet count of 63,000/mm3). Mean platelet volume was 4.8 fL.
